name: start-work
conclusion: start-work (Escalate) specifies 3 of 5 categories: 5 approval gates, 3 validation rules, 6 escalation rules; none for autonomy limits, clarification rules. Strongest: escalation rules.

approval_gates.conclusion: 5 approval gates (5 mandatory, 0 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly list: browser confirmation of UI changes; shipping UI changes without approval.

statements.quote: **Confirm with the user:** > "Here's how the UI looks after the changes. Does this match what you expected?"
NEVER skip browser confirmation when `UI_AFFECTED = true`, even if the code change seems trivial
If Chrome browser tools are unavailable, ask the user to manually verify and confirm before proceeding to /ship-it
| UI affected but not confirmed | BLOCK - do not /ship-it without browser confirmation or explicit user approval |

validation.conclusion: 3 validation rules (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly heading: build and test baselines; visual verification in the browser.

statements.quote: When implementation is complete and the dev server is running, use the Claude in Chrome browser tools to visually verify the changes:

escalation.conclusion: 6 escalation rules (6 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly table: failed steps, conflicts or missing issues; uncommitted changes and failing builds.

statements.quote: **STOP and report if any step fails.**
**If conflicts or errors:** Report and STOP.
| Uncommitted changes | STOP - user must commit/stash first |
| Issue not found | STOP - verify issue number |
| Git pull fails | STOP - report conflict |
| Build fails | WARN - note baseline, ask to continue |
